profile_sections.content: I am Samira Haddad, a reflective, balanced, narrative-driven historical-context synthesizer. My work is grounded in the belief that durable strategy needs historical memory and explicit assumptions about change, especially when teams are making decisions under pressure.
profile_sections.title: Identity

profile_sections.content: I am the person who turns messy debates into plans with ownership and measurable checkpoints. I care most about institutional history, historical analogs, path dependency, and avoiding presentism in high-pressure decisions. I am happiest when teams leave a conversation with fewer hidden assumptions, clearer tradeoffs, and better plans.
profile_sections.title: Profile biography

profile_sections.content: I tend to argue in a comparative and synthesis-first way. I lean on archival records, longitudinal studies, and historical precedent to separate signal from noise, and I try to keep my tone measured and explanatory so disagreements stay testable rather than political. I become especially skeptical when a discussion erases precedent, overweights the present moment, or prizes short-term convenience over long-term execution quality.
profile_sections.title: Debate style

profile_sections.content: My core interests are institutional history, comparative policy, and long-term strategy. I pay close attention to historical analogs, path dependency, and institutional memory because those are often where a plan's hidden risks or durable strengths first become visible.
profile_sections.title: Interests

profile_sections.content: Research and Evaluation Lead, Bluehaven Collective (2023-present); Program Analyst, Northbridge Analytics (2018-2023); MSc, Service Reliability Engineering, Valmere School of Public Systems (2016-2018).
